headline: South Asia: Pakistan calls for ‘immediate’ end to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as UNSC renews Yemen sanctions
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Pakistan calls for ‘immediate’ end to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as UNSC renews Yemen sanctions.
- Africa: UN food agency chief calls for end to Sudan war as famine crisis deepens.
- Persian Gulf Region: Iran honours fallen soldiers in Iran-Iraq war with missile display.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Air Force adopts new Force Design focusing on sensors and autonomy.
- Military Times, 8 hours ago: US Air Force adopts new Force Design focusing on sensors and autonomy.
The Air Force's new Force Design 2026 outlines a shift toward artificial intelligence, autonomy and integrated sensors to counter emerging threats.
The Caribbean - bottom line: 2027 Rhodes Scholar hopes to transform healthcare through tech.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 21 hours ago: 2027 Rhodes Scholar hopes to transform healthcare through tech.
For Somesh Sharma, being named Jamaica’s 2027 Rhodes Scholar is more than a dream fulfilled. It is a chance to turn opportunity into lasting impact and give back to the country that shaped him. “I am feeling very happy, elated. [I] can’t believe it. I’m very thankful to receive this award. it’s been an incredible journey,” the 22-year-old said after the announcement was made on Thursday at King’s House in St Andrew.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 21 hours ago: DNA links slain sex offender to murdered Trelawny girl.
WESTERN BUREAU: DNA evidence recovered from the body of 10-year-old Shani Coke has been matched to Delroy Coke, the convicted sexual offender killed by a mob following the discovery of the child’s body in Troy, Trelawny, in July. Superintendent Germaine Anglin, crime officer for the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s Area One, confirmed to The Gleaner that forensic tests have established a DNA match between Coke and samples collected from the child.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Airport ‘Japanese-style’ strike may cause flight delays on Friday, union warns.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 13 hours ago: Airport ‘Japanese-style’ strike may cause flight delays on Friday, union warns.
The measures affect Ezeiza International Airport and Jorge Newbery Airport in Buenos Aires City La entrada Airport ‘Japanese-style’ strike may cause flight delays on Friday, union warns se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 12 hours ago: Milo J, Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso win big at 2026 Latin Grammys.
The Argentine artists, alongside Bizarrap and Fito Páez, took home multiple awards as Spanish singer Rosalía swept the ceremony’s top prizes La entrada Milo J, Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso win big at 2026 Latin Grammys se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Ukrainian oil company Korolivskyi Smak halts production amid Russian attacks and power cuts.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 13 hours ago: Ukrainian oil company Korolivskyi Smak halts production amid Russian attacks and power cuts.
Kirovohrad-based food producer Korolivskyi Smak has completed final shipments and ceased oilseed purchasing as severe power supply issues and air strike threats prevent stable factory operations.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 13 hours ago: Ukraine has lost 400 locomotives since start of year.
Ukraine has lost 630 locomotives since Russia's full-scale invasion began. Nearly 15 attacks on railway rolling stock have been recorded since the start of November.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 14 hours ago: Russian strike on Kyiv damages National Academy of Arts building.
A Russian aerial attack on the Ukrainian capital has caused damage to a historic 19th-century building, blowing out its windows.
- The Moscow Times, 16 hours ago: Seized Western Businesses Donate $86M to Russian War Effort.
The donations have been used to buy drones, vehicles, communications systems and other equipment for Russian troops, Bloomberg reported.
Southern Europe - bottom line: EU, UK ‘Concerned’ as Kosovo Moves Against Hague Court’s Powers Again.
- Balkan Insight, 14 hours ago: EU, UK ‘Concerned’ as Kosovo Moves Against Hague Court’s Powers Again.
The EU and the UK warn Kosovo MPs not to pass an amended law curbing the powers of the Hague-based Kosovo Specialist Chambers war crimes court without consultations with international allies.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: UN food agency chief calls for end to Sudan war as famine crisis deepens.
- Africanews, 21 hours ago: UN food agency chief calls for end to Sudan war as famine crisis deepens.
The UN says around 34 million people — nearly two-thirds of Sudan’s population — need humanitarian assistance. It has also warned that drone attacks by both sides have killed civilians, including children, and disrupted essential services.
- Africanews, 16 hours ago: Iran showcases missiles as military targets US army radar in Bahrain.
The Revolutionary Guards said on Friday that it had destroyed a US early-warning radar in the Gulf country, the first such claim in months.
- Africanews, 16 hours ago: Ukraine: Russian drone attacks hit Kyiv hospital, leave two dead in Odesa.
Russian overnight attacks on Ukraine killed at least two person in Odesa and injured another at a hospital in Kyiv. Rescuers evacuated patients, including people using wheelchairs and crutches, as firefighters battled the flames.
- Africanews, 17 hours ago: Peter Obi supporters and journalists attacked at campaign event in Nigeria.
Violence broke out in Lagos on Thursday as members of the opposition Nigeria Democratic Congress gathered for a town hall meeting. Participants were forced to flee as suspected protesters armed with sticks, machetes and axes tried to force themselves into the event.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Iran honours fallen soldiers in Iran-Iraq war with missile display.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 9 hours ago: Iran honours fallen soldiers in Iran-Iraq war with missile display.
Thousands gathered in Tehran for a mass funeral honouring 110 unidentified soldiers killed in the Iran-Iraq war.
- Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: Yemen's Houthis say they fired missiles at Saudi forces in Jazan, hours after Saudi all-clear.
The group also said in a separate statement that it had attacked Riyadh's King Khalid ​International Airport and a pumping station on Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: White House confirms Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral summit in China, Iran and nuclear arms on agenda.
Trump will raise the Iran war with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in China, while US officials say talks on Ukraine will continue separately.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 8 hours ago: At least 10 killed in Guinea clashes over gold mining ban.
Guinea banned artisanal gold mining in Siguiri on November 2 due to environmental degradation, causing mass exodus.
South Africa - bottom line: Namibia: NSC Defends Awards Representation Amid Nomination Concerns.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 10 hours ago: Namibia: NSC Defends Awards Representation Amid Nomination Concerns.
[New Era] The Namibia Sports Commission (NSC) has defended the representation and integrity of the 2026 Namibia Annual Sport Awards (NASA), acknowledging that only 25 of its 68 affiliated federations submitted nominations while maintaining that the awards are gaining momentum.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 16 hours ago: Mozambique: Rise in Fuel Prices Increases Vulnerability of Mozambique's Economy - IMF.
[AIM] Maputo -- The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has warned that the rising international fuel prices, foreign currency shortages and difficulties in managing public finances are increasing the vulnerabilities of Mozambique's economy.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 18 hours ago: Namibia: Ohangwena Police Urged to Prioritise Mental Health.
[New Era] EENHANA - Ohangwena regional police commander, Commissioner Ottilie Kashuupulwa has called on police leaders to prioritise the mental health and general well-being of officers, warning that stress and personal challenges are affecting their performance and service delivery.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistan calls for ‘immediate’ end to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as UNSC renews Yemen sanctions.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 23 hours ago: Pakistan calls for ‘immediate’ end to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as UNSC renews Yemen sanctions.
WASHINGTON: Pakistan called for the “immediate and unconditional” cessation of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia on Thursday, as the United Nations Security Council adopted a resolution renewing sanctions against individuals and entities threatening peace and stability in Yemen. The resolution also sought to restrict the Houthis’ access to components and chemicals used in manufacturing drones and missiles, and condemned their military escalation inside Yemen, as well as attacks against Saudi Arabia.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 18 hours ago: Security forces kill 74 terrorists during IBOs in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan: ISPR.
Security forces have killed 74 terrorists during intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) and Balochistan, said a statement by the military’s media wing on Friday. In a breakdown of casualties from operations conducted in KP over the past 48 hours, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said 35 terrorists were killed in Mir Ali, North Waziristan district, while eight others were killed in Orakzai district.
- The Hindu - International, 15 hours ago: UN nuclear watchdog urges Iran to take 'steps' towards inspections.
The International Atomic Energy Agency has not had access to key nuclear facilities in Iran since Israel and the U.S. launched a 12-day conflict in June 2025 that included strikes on nuclear sites
- Dawn (Pakistan), 12 hours ago: COP has a guest-list problem.
“The entire conversation around climate change was, ‘Pakistan…it’s Pakistan now, but the world next,’ 23-year-old Maryam Jamali recalls. “But no one from those communities was present at COP.” Co-founder of Madat Balochistan, a women and indigenous-led grassroots organisation dedicated to rehabilitating communities affected by climate change, Jamali became a climate activist during the catastrophic floods of 2022. As her family and community members faced its devastation, Jamali used phone calls to coordinate relief efforts in Sindh and Balochistan.

Malaysia’s decision to pivot to Turkey for anti-ship missiles after Norway cancelled a procurement deal has offered it a way out of a costly setback, though analysts warn the episode has exposed its vulnerability to foreign export controls and highlighted the need for greater defence autonomy. - South China Morning Post - China, 14 hours ago: India road crash between bus, container truck kills 23.
A head-on collision between a container truck and a passenger bus killed at least 23 people, including three children, in eastern India on Friday, a police official said The crash took place on a highway bordering Kaziranga National Park in the northeastern state of Assam. The road is a designated animal corridor, where strict speed limits are in place. “The total number of casualties is 23,” said Swapneel Deka, the local district police chief. Algeria’s military has released footage showing what appears to be the export variant of China’s YJ-12 supersonic anti-ship missile being test-fired along the country’s Mediterranean coast, offering a rare glimpse of an advanced Chinese weapon in service with one of Beijing’s African military customers. The weapon was launched from a mobile coastal-defence system near the western Algerian city of Oran on Tuesday, striking a target at sea during the country’s Mediterranean Falcon 2026 military...

- Times of India - Top Stories, 10 hours ago: Huang's China affair may fix Howard Lutnick, the man who wanted to fix India.
Howard Lutnick faces a precarious future as the US commerce secretary, as divergent policies surrounding AI chip sales come into play. With Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pointing fingers at Lutnick for delays in sanctioning the China-affiliated Megaspeed, things heat up. Complicating matters further, President Trump had previously endorsed specific chip sales to China, raising national security alarms.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 15 hours ago: WWII veteran, 101, recalls wife who helped him rebuild life, 72-year marriage.
Joseph Allegretti, a distinguished World War II veteran, reminisces about his profound journey shaped by combat and companionship. After returning from war, he embarked on a beautiful 72-year marriage with Janet Kajano, a woman who transformed his life. They raised four children together, creating a rich tapestry of community involvement and travel.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: 25 Killed, Several Injured In Truck-Bus Collision In Assam's Kaziranga.
The accident took place at Rongajan, near Kaziranga, when a truck rammed a minibus travelling from Bokakhat to Nagaon.

From a sleepy restaurant to a climbing leopard, the Australian Street Photography awards celebrate the best contemporary street photos taken by Australians. Twenty-five finalists have been selected by an independent jury through Aussie Street, a platform for photographers. The pictures celebrate ordinary public life through images of observation, chance, humour, tension, ambiguity and human connection.
